result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter gives the results of your knee scan (MRI). The scan was of your left knee. It was done on 1 September 2026.

- You may have a small tear in part of your knee (the posterior horn of the medial meniscus). This is possible. The scan cannot rule out a tear.
- There is no fracture (broken bone).
- Your ligament (anterior cruciate ligament, ACL) is intact.
- You have mild early wear and tear (degenerative changes, osteoarthritis). It is on the inner side of the knee (medial compartment).
- You have a little fluid in the knee (small joint effusion).
- Surgery is not planned at this stage.

## What you need to do
1. You can continue normal activities as pain allows.
2. Your doctor has referred you for physiotherapy. It is for 6 to 8 weeks. The letter does not say when it starts.
3. The consultant will see you in the orthopaedic clinic in 3 months. The letter does not give a date.

## Dates and medicines
- 1 September 2026: MRI of your left knee was done.
- 6 to 8 weeks: physiotherapy. The referral is made.
- In 3 months: review in the orthopaedic clinic with the consultant.
- Medicines: the letter lists no medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will my physiotherapy start?
- What date is my clinic review in 3 months?
- What does "possible tear" mean for me?
- How much activity is right for my knee?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
